frequency_question: How often do high-complexity defense technology transfers and domestic manufacturing setups succeed within a 2-to-3-year window when backed by maximum political will?
membership_rule: Includes instances of foreign-origin missile or precision weapon systems where a recipient nation attempted to stand up local assembly/production lines. Excludes standard small arms, basic artillery shells, or unguided munitions.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng III domestic production scaling
South Korea Taurus KEPD 350 integration/licensing attempt
Turkey SOM cruise missile domestic industrialization
Ukraine R-360 Neptune domestic missile serial production initiation

coverage_note: 5 named major sovereign missile localization programs with clear historical records of completion or failure within the defined technological category.
known_gaps: Classified or highly covert wartime co-production arrangements (e.g., recent Middle Eastern or Eastern European initiatives) are under-reported in open sources.
skeleton: Cases of complex missile technology domestic production establishment under various urgency levels.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 named reference cases
validity_reason: Defense industrial base constraints, intellectual property protections, and high-precision machining bottlenecks evolve slowly over decades.
